items.title: Louis Armstrong Interview, 1960-08-16
items.q: even when I joined Fletcher Henderson at the Roseland Ballroom I was just 24 years old and in that band you had Colvin Hawkins, Don Redmond, Kaiser Marshall, Fletcher at the piano, Joe Smith you know we had some band Pete Charlie Green with it

ctx.x: well then apparently he didn't learn it anywhere he had it

but it's in him yeah and but the average kid would say I don't want to play that I want to play uh uh uh uh I'm with you on that you know when I was a teenager I listened to the good old greats you know what I mean the boys around my crowd was gonna go to the next neighborhood and fight and all that you know what I mean so I thought they were stupid see I want to hear the elders of people and what they talked about in music and everything like that even when I joined Fletcher Henderson at the Roseland Ballroom I…
working with men that are better than you and I guess there was a time when there was someone better than you when you were awfully young.

items.title: Louis Armstrong: Jazz Casual Interview, 1964-07-10
items.q: Well, they always had their own band, like Coleman Hawkins. Used to play with Mamie Smith.

ctx.x: All right. Yeah. With singers like Ma Rainey, did they ever appear in the places where you played with Oliver? Oh, well, not at the Lincoln Gardens.

They didn't. I mean, they're always in the theaters, and the crowd's standing around the corner to get in. Yeah. Like Bessie Smith, Mamie Smith, and Clara Smith, and Miss Barnes, what is her name? She was in, no, she made this good time flat blues. All that. Yeah. Yeah. Well, they always had their own band, like Coleman Hawkins. Used to play with Mamie Smith.
Well, when they started to make these records, and you made a whole series of records accompanying singers, how did they bring you in? Did they heard you?
